writeup.headline: Dave rates Buy on very strong quality, a clean balance sheet and fast but slowing growth.
writeup.thesis: Dave scores 71, a Buy, carried mainly by quality (93) and balance sheet (90). It has a free cash flow margin of 50.7%, stock-based pay at 5.8% of revenue and a diluted share count down 6.0% year on year, while net debt is just 0.05 times free cash flow. Growth scores 69 on TTM revenue growth of 48.6% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 29.6% year on year, though growth slowed by 17.1 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation (63) is moderate in absolute terms at 6.9x sales and 13.5x free cash flow, with FCF yield 2.4 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield; against its own history it is near the middle overall, with P/S more expensive than at 34 of the last 44 month-ends. Trend (61) and news risk (54) are middling: the price is 27.1% below its 52-week high and 8.9% below its 50-day average, but shares are 16.4 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Revenue growth is decelerating sharply, with growth slowed by 17.1 pp from the previous quarter.
The pending FTC/DOJ case over ExtraCash and the Baltimore suit could hit its core product.
It depends on the Coastal Community Bank partnership.
Q3 results on 2026-11-04 could reset expectations after the August guidance raise.
Weak recent price action: the price is 27.1% below its 52-week high and 8.9% below its 50-day average.
what_would_change: A gain of 9 points, for example from re-accelerating growth or a recovering trend, would lift the rating to Strong Buy.
A loss of 7 points would drop it to Hold, for instance if growth keeps slowing or the trend weakens further.
An adverse ruling or settlement in the FTC/DOJ ExtraCash case would likely push news risk down.
A rise in P/S further above its own history without matching growth would weigh on the valuation score.
